title: Family of Hyderabad Man Killed in Riyadh Airport Attack Will Hold Funeral in Saudi Arabia
excerpt: Mohammed Yousuf Ali, 46, was killed travelling to Medina for Umrah. The Indian Embassy says it is completing funeral formalities in Riyadh while five injured Indians remain in intensive care.
body:
• The family of Mohammed Yousuf Ali, the Hyderabad IT professional killed in Saturday's attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, has decided to hold his funeral in Riyadh.
  • The Indian Embassy says it is completing all funeral formalities and remains in constant touch with the injured Indians' families.
  • Of the injured Indian nationals, three remain in ICU and two more have been admitted to ICU; two are in a normal ward and the rest have been discharged.
  • Ali, 46, had worked in Riyadh for a decade and was travelling with his wife and three children to Medina for Umrah when the attack struck.

Funeral in Riyadh, embassy handling formalities

The family of Mohammed Yousuf Ali, the Indian national killed in the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, has decided to conduct his funeral in the Saudi capital, the Indian Embassy said on Monday. The mission said it is providing all assistance to the bereaved family, including completion of all formalities for the funeral.

Ali, a 46-year-old IT professional from Hyderabad's Mehdipatnam area, had been employed in Riyadh for about a decade. His wife and three children had arrived in Saudi Arabia roughly ten days earlier, and the family was waiting in the airport lounge for a flight to Medina, where they were travelling for Umrah, when debris from the strike hit the terminal area.

The injured: sons in surgery, five Indians in ICU

Embassy officials have visited the hospitals treating the injured Indian nationals. In its latest update, the mission said three persons continue in intensive care and two more have been admitted to ICU, two remain in a normal ward, and the rest have been discharged. In Ali's own family, his 18-year-old son Aman underwent knee surgery, and his 16-year-old son Wasi lost three toes; his wife Sameera and 11-year-old daughter Maryam sustained minor injuries. Another Telangana resident, Shaik Saeed, 42, from Kamareddy district, who worked at a cafe inside the airport, was also injured and admitted to ICU at King Fahad Military Hospital, according to reports from Hyderabad.

Hyderabad MP Asaduddin Owaisi said he had spoken to the family's relatives and to the embassy's deputy chief of mission, and had asked External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar to ensure the family receives full assistance.

The attack and what families should know

Saudi Arabia has blamed Yemen's Houthi movement for the attack on the civilian airport, which killed people of several nationalities — among them four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a US citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese — and injured around 300, including ten Indian nationals, according to the embassy. India has strongly condemned the attack on civilian infrastructure.

Indian nationals in Saudi Arabia should follow the Indian Embassy in Riyadh's updates and the stay-indoors advisory issued after the attack, and avoid airport areas while Saudi authorities warn of further strikes. Our earlier coverage of the casualties and the advisory is here: One Indian Dead, Three in ICU After Riyadh Airport Attack. The embassy's statement is carried in full by The Daily Jagran.
